<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:2.52%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred Revenues</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.2%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s deferred revenues consist primarily of gift card liabilities, certain incentive liabilities as well as customer billings for professional services recognized ratably over the subscription period. These amounts are included within other accruals on the consolidated balance sheets. See Note 8, <span style="font-style:italic;">Other Accruals</span>, for the Company&#8217;s gift card liabilities as of <span style="color:#000000;">December 31, 2019</span> and 2018. Other deferred revenues are not material to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position. The majority of gift cards and incentives issued by the Company are redeemed within a year.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:2.52%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Contract Acquisition Costs</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.2%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company defers the incremental costs of obtaining and renewing restaurant and corporate and campus program customer contracts, primarily consisting of commissions and bonuses and related payroll taxes, as contract acquisition assets within other assets on the consolidated balance sheets. Contract acquisition assets are amortized on a straight-line basis to sales and marketing expense in the consolidated statements of operations over the useful life of the contract, which is estimated to be approximately <span><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000486" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000487" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_20181231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> years</span> based on anticipated customer renewals.&#160;During the years ended <span style="color:#000000;">December 31, 2019</span> and 2018, the Company deferred $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000488" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostGross" contextRef="C_0001594109_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">16.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000489" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostGross" contextRef="C_0001594109_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="6">10.3</ix:nonFraction> million of contract acquisitions costs, respectively, and amortized $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000490" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortization" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.5</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000491" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortization" contextRef="C_0001594109_20180101_20181231" decimals="INF" scale="6">1.3</ix:nonFraction> million of related expense, respectively. </p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">51</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">GRUBHUB INC.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000365" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000365_dcnt_f45f13b9-90ae-4b21-aba4-aea77df974d5">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">4. Acquisitions </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no acquisitions during the year ended December 31, 2019</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">2018 Acquisitions</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.71%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000492" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEffectiveDateOfAcquisition1" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181106_20181107" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">November 7, 2018</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company acquired all of the issued and outstanding shares of Tapingo Ltd. (&#8220;Tapingo&#8221;) for approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000493" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredGoodwillAndLiabilitiesAssumedNet" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">152.1</ix:nonFraction> million, including $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000494" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181106_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">151.7</ix:nonFraction> million of cash paid (net of cash acquired of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000495" name="us-gaap:CashAcquiredFromAcquisition" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181106_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">1.5</ix:nonFraction> million) and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000496" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferredEquityInterestsIssuedAndIssuable" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_grubIncentiveStockOptionMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181106_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million of other non-cash consideration. Tapingo is a leading platform for campus food ordering with direct integration into college meal plans and point of sale systems. The acquisition of Tapingo has enhanced the Company&#8217;s diner network on college campuses.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.71%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000497" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEffectiveDateOfAcquisition1" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180912_20180913" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">September 13, 2018</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company acquired SCVNGR, Inc. d/b/a LevelUp (&#8220;LevelUp&#8221;) for approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000498" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredGoodwillAndLiabilitiesAssumedNet" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180913" decimals="-5" scale="6">369.4</ix:nonFraction> million, including $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000499" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180912_20180913" decimals="-5" scale="6">366.8</ix:nonFraction> million of cash paid (net of cash acquired of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000500" name="us-gaap:CashAcquiredFromAcquisition" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180912_20180913" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.0</ix:nonFraction> million) and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000501" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferredEquityInterestsIssuedAndIssuable" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_grubIncentiveStockOptionMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180912_20180913" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million of other non-cash consideration.&#160;<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#222222;">LevelUp is a leading provider of mobile diner engagement and payment solutions for national and regional restaurant brands. The acquisition of LevelUp has simplified the Company&#8217;s integrations with restaurants&#8217; systems, increased diner engagement and accelerated product development.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.71%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company assumed Tapingo and LevelUp employees&#8217; unvested incentive stock option (&#8220;ISO&#8221;) awards as of the respective closing dates. Approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000502" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferredEquityInterestsIssuedAndIssuable" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_grubIncentiveStockOptionMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoLtdMember_20181106_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000503" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferredEquityInterestsIssuedAndIssuable" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_grubIncentiveStockOptionMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubLevelUpMember_20180912_20180913" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.6</ix:nonFraction> million of the fair value of the assumed ISO awards granted to acquired Tapingo and LevelUp employees, respectively, was attributable to the pre-combination services of the awardees and was included in the respective purchase prices. These amounts are reflected within goodwill in the respective purchase price allocations. As of the respective acquisition dates, aggregate post-combination expense of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000504" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedStockOptions" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_grubIncentiveStockOptionMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoAndLevelUpMember_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">21.4</ix:nonFraction> million was expected to be recognized related to the combined assumed ISO awards over the remaining post-combination service periods.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.71%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The results of operations of Tapingo and LevelUp have been included in the Company&#8217;s financial statements since November 7, 2018 and September 13, 2018, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.71%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The excess of the consideration transferred in the acquisitions over the amounts assigned to the fair value of the net assets acquired was recorded as goodwill, which represents the value&#160;of LevelUp&#8217;s technology team, the ability to simplify integrations with restaurants on the Company&#8217;s platform and the expanded breadth and depth of the Company&#8217;s network of diners and campus relationships. The total goodwill related to the acquisitions of Tapingo and LevelUp of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000505" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubTapingoAndLevelUpMember_20181107" decimals="-5" scale="6">418.1</ix:nonFraction> million is not deductible for income tax purposes.</p>

This amount is reflected within goodwill in the purchase price allocation. As of the acquisition date, post-combination expense of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000550" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognizedStockOptions" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubEatTwentyFourLLCMember_20171010" decimals="-5" scale="6">4.1</ix:nonFraction> million was expected to be recognized related to the replacement awards over the remaining post-combination service period.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000551" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEffectiveDateOfAcquisition1" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubFoodlerMember_20170822_20170823" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">August 23, 2017</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company acquired substantially all of the assets and certain expressly specified liabilities of A&#38;D Network Solutions, Inc. and Dashed, Inc. (collectively, &#8220;Foodler&#8221;). The purchase price for Foodler was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000552" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubFoodlerMember_20170822_20170823" decimals="-5" scale="6">51.1</ix:nonFraction> million in cash, net of cash acquired of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000553" name="us-gaap:CashAcquiredFromAcquisition" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubFoodlerMember_20170822_20170823" decimals="-5" scale="6">0.1</ix:nonFraction> million. Foodler is an independent online food-ordering company with an established diner base in the Northeast United States. The acquisition expanded the breadth and depth of the Company&#8217;s restaurant network, active diners and delivery network.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The results of operations of Eat24 and Foodler have been included in the Company&#8217;s financial statements since October 10, 2017 and August 23, 2017, respectively.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The excess of the consideration transferred in the acquisitions over the net amounts assigned to the fair value of the assets was recorded as goodwill, <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">which represents the value of increasing the breadth and depth of the Company&#8217;s network of restaurants and diners</span>. The total goodwill related to the acquisitions of Eat24 and Foodler of $<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000554">153.4</span> million is expected to be deductible for income tax purposes.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The assets acquired and liabilities assumed of Eat24 and Foodler were recorded at their estimated fair values as of the respective closing dates of October 10, 2017 and August 23, 2017. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000405" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfRecognizedIdentifiedAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapBusinessAcquisitionAxis_grubEatTwentyFourAndFoodlerMember_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000405_cnt_1">The following table summarizes the final purchase price allocation acquisition-date fair values of the assets and liabilities acquired in connection with the Eat24 and Foodler acquisitions:</ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="F_000405_cnt_1">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> The fair value of the LevelUp below-market lease was measured based on the present value of the difference between the contractual amounts to be paid pursuant to the lease and an estimate of current fair market lease rates measured over the non-cancelable remaining term of the lease. As of January 1, 2019, the below-market lease intangible asset was derecognized from acquired intangible assets resulting in a corresponding adjustment to the opening balance of operating lease right-of-use assets on the consolidated balance sheets upon adoption of ASC Topic 842.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These fair value measurements were based on significant inputs not observable in the market and thus represent Level 3 measurements within the fair value hierarchy. Unobservable inputs were reflective of the types of assumptions that market participants would use in measuring the fair values of similar assets and liabilities such as, among others, discount rates, estimated future cash flows, initial developer costs, expected profits, royalty rates, rates of attrition and expected rates of return. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company incurred certain expenses directly and indirectly related to acquisitions <span style="color:#000000;">of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000604" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenseMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">2.7</ix:nonFraction></span> million, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000605" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenseMember_20180101_20181231" decimals="-5" scale="6">6.9</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000606" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" contextRef="C_0001594109_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenseMember_20170101_20171231" decimals="-5" scale="6">5.6</ix:nonFraction> million which were recognized in general and administrative expenses within the consolidated statements of operations for the years ended December 31, 2019, 2018 and 2017, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;<span style="font-weight:bold;">9. Commitments and Contingencies </span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.72%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Leases</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.92%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000803" name="us-gaap:DescriptionOfLesseeLeasingArrangementsOperatingLeases" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231">As of&#160;December 31, 2019, the Company had operating lease agreements for its office facilities in various locations throughout the U.S, as well as in the U.K. and Israel, which expire at various dates through May 2030.&#160;</ix:nonNumeric>The terms of the lease agreements provide for fixed rental payments on a graduated basis. For its primary operating leases, the Company can, after the initial lease term, renew its leases under right of first offer terms at fair value at the time of renewal for a period of&#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000802" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRenewalTerm" contextRef="C_0001594109_20191231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric>. &#160;The Company's lease terms include options to extend or terminate the lease when it is reasonably certain that it will exercise that option.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Legal </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.19%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2011, Ameranth, Inc. (&#8220;Ameranth&#8221;) filed a patent infringement action against a number of defendants, including Grubhub Holdings Inc., in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of California, Case No.&#160;3:11-cv-1810. Ameranth subsequently initiated additional actions for infringement of a related patent, including separate actions against Grubhub Holdings Inc., Case No. 3:12-cv-739, and Seamless North America, LLC, Case No. 3:12-cv-737, which were consolidated along with approximately 40 other cases Ameranth filed in the same district.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2018, the district court granted summary judgment (on another defendant&#8217;s motion) of unpatentability on the sole remaining patent and vacated the December 3, 2018 jury trial date for the claims against Grubhub Holdings Inc. and Seamless North America, LLC.&#160;In October 2018, the district court entered final judgment on all claims in the case in which summary judgment was granted, and then stayed the remaining cases (including the cases against Grubhub and Seamless). Ameranth then appealed this decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. In November 2019, the Federal Circuit affirmed the district court&#8217;s findings of unpatentability in all material respects, and remanded certain dependent claims to the district court. The Company believes this case lacks merit and that it has strong defenses to all of the infringement claims. The Company intends to defend the suit vigorously. The Company has not recorded an accrual related to this lawsuit as of&#160;<span style="color:#000000;">December 31, 2019</span>,&#160;as it does not believe a material loss is probable.</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">On November 20, 2019, a purported stockholder of the Company filed a putative class action complaint against the Company, Chief Executive Officer Matthew Maloney, and Chief Financial Officer Adam DeWitt in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, Case No. 19 Civ. 7665.&#160;&#160;The complaint asserts violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 10b-5 promulgated thereunder, based on its allegation that the defendants made false and misleading statements about the Company&#8217;s growth, competitive landscape, and strategy.&#160;&#160;The complaint seeks unspecified compensatory damages and attorneys&#8217; fees, among other relief.&#160;&#160;The defendants believe that the complaint is without merit.&#160;&#160;A reasonable estimate of the amount of any possible loss or range of loss cannot be made at this time.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.88%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">In addition to the matters described above, from&#160;time to time, the Company is involved in various other legal proceedings arising from the normal course of business activities, including&#160;labor and employment claims, some of which relate to the alleged misclassification of independent contractors.&#160;In September 2015, a claim was brought in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California under the Private Attorneys General Act by an individual plaintiff on behalf of himself and seeking to represent other drivers and the State of California. The claim sought monetary penalties and injunctive relief for alleged violations of the California Labor Code based on the alleged misclassification of drivers as independent contractors.&#160;</span>A decision was issued on February 8, 2018, and the court ruled in favor of the Company, finding that plaintiff was properly classified as an independent contractor.&#160;In March 2018, the plaintiff appealed this decision to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.&#160;Several other putative class actions and arbitrations have been brought against the Company alleging misclassification of independent contractors. <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">The Company does not believe any of the foregoing claims will have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements. However,&#160;</span>there is no assurance that any claim will not be combined into a collective or class action.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Indemnification</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with the merger of Seamless North America, LLC, Seamless Holdings Corporation and Grubhub Holdings Inc. in August 2013, the Company agreed to indemnify Aramark Holdings Corporation for negative income tax consequences associated with the October 2012 spin-off of Seamless Holdings Corporation that were the result of certain actions taken by the Company through October 29, 2014, in certain instances subject to a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000835" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyEstimateOfPossibleLoss" contextRef="C_0001594109_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapLossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis_grubMergerIncomeTaxConsequencesMember_20191231" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.0</ix:nonFraction> million limitation. Management is not aware of any actions that would impact the indemnification obligation.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11. Stock-Based Compensation </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has granted non-qualified and incentive stock options, restricted stock units and restricted stock awards under its incentive plans. The Company recognizes compensation expense based on estimated grant date fair values for all stock-based awards issued to employees and directors, including stock options, restricted stock units and restricted stock awards. For all stock options outstanding as of December&#160;31, 2019, the exercise price of the stock options equals the fair value of the stock option on the grant date. The stock options and restricted stock units vest over different lengths of time, but generally over <span><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000908" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000909" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> years</span>, and are subject to forfeiture upon termination of employment prior to vesting. The maximum term for stock options issued to employees under the 2015 Plan, the 2013 Plan and the assumed Tapingo and LevelUp incentive plans is <span><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000905" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000906" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000907" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric> years</span>, and they expire <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000910" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardExpirationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years from the date of grant. Compensation expense for stock options, restricted stock units and restricted stock awards is recognized ratably over the vesting period. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The rights granted to the recipient of a restricted stock unit generally accrue over the vesting period. Participants holding restricted stock units are not entitled to any ordinary cash dividends paid by the Company with respect to such shares. The Company does not expect to pay any dividends in the foreseeable future.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:14.66%;text-indent:-4.58%;font-size:1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">__________________________________________________________________________________________________</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s tax returns are subject to the normal statute of limitations, three years from the filing date for federal income tax purposes. The federal and state statute of limitations generally remain open for years in which tax losses are generated until three years from the year those losses are utilized. Under these rules, the 2006 and later year NOLs of Slick City Media, Inc. are still subject to audit by the IRS and state and local jurisdictions. Also, the 2007 and later year NOLs of Grubhub Holdings Inc. and its acquired businesses are still subject to audit by the IRS and state and local jurisdictions. The December 31, 2016 and later period U.K. returns of Seamless Europe Ltd. are subject to examination by the U.K. tax authorities. The December 31, 2015 and later period Israeli returns of Tapingo Ltd. are subject to exam by the Israeli tax authorities. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is subject to taxation in the U.S. federal and various state jurisdictions. Significant judgment is required in determining the provision for income taxes and recording the related income tax assets and liabilities. The Company&#8217;s practice for accounting for uncertainty in income taxes is to recognize the financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more likely than not sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more-likely-than-not criteria, the amount recognized in the financial statements is the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. </p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000432" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsRollForwardTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.58%;text-indent:-4.58%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:9pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000376" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001594109_20190101_20191231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000376_dcnt_c8ade582-133c-4b76-a73e-9e31fd09e485">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15. Earnings Per Share Attributable to Common Stockholders </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing net income (loss) attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period without consideration for common stock equivalents. Diluted net income per share attributable to common stockholders is computed by dividing net income by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the period and potentially dilutive common stock equivalents, including stock options and restricted stock units, except in cases where the effect of the common stock equivalent would be antidilutive. Potential common stock equivalents consist of common stock issuable upon exercise of stock options and vesting of restricted stock units using the treasury stock method. <span style="color:#000000;">For periods of net loss, basic and diluted earnings per share are the same as the effect of the assumed exercise of stock options and vesting of restricted stock units is anti-dilutive.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The sale of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001165" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesNewIssues" contextRef="C_0001594109_srtOwnershipAxis_grubAccreditedInvestorMember_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapCommonStockMember_us-gaapTypeOfArrangementAxis_grubInvestmentAgreementMember_20180425_20180425" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,820,464</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock to the Investor on April 25, 2018 resulted in an immediate increase in the outstanding shares used to calculate the weighted-average common shares outstanding for the year&#160;ended December 31, 2018 (see Note 13, <span style="font-style:italic;">Stockholders' Equity</span>).</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">67</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">16. Fair Value Measurement </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain assets and liabilities are required to be recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. Accounting standards define fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date. The standards also establish a fair value hierarchy, which requires an entity to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when measuring fair value. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accounting guidance for fair value measurements prioritizes valuation methodologies based on the reliability of the inputs in the following three-tier value hierarchy: </p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.58%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.14%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;1</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.58%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.14%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;2</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Assets and liabilities valued based on observable market data for similar instruments, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.58%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.14%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;3</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity&#59; instruments valued based on the best available data, some of which is internally developed, and considers risk premiums that a market participant would require.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company applied the following methods and assumptions in estimating its fair value measurements. The Company&#8217;s commercial paper, investments in corporate bonds, certain money market funds and Senior Notes are classified as Level 2 within the fair value hierarchy because they are valued using inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are observable directly or indirectly. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s outstanding borrowings under the Credit Agreement as of December 31, 2018 was classified as Level 3 within the fair value hierarchy because it was valued using an income approach, which utilized a discounted </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">68</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Grubhub Inc. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Chicago, Illinois</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Opinion on the Financial Statements</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:3.49%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Grubhub Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) as of December 31, 2019 and 2018, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), changes in stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2019, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;financial statements&#8221;). In our opinion,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.85pt;"> </span>financial<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>statements<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>present<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>fairly,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>all<span style="letter-spacing:-0.85pt;"> </span>material<span style="letter-spacing:-0.85pt;"> </span>respects,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>financial<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>position<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>Company as<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>December<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>31,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>2019<span style="letter-spacing:-0.3pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>2018,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>results<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>its<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>operations<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>its<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>cash<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>flows<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>for<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>each<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>three years<span style="letter-spacing:-0.15pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.15pt;"> </span>period<span style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </span>ended<span style="letter-spacing:-0.3pt;"> </span>December<span style="letter-spacing:-0.25pt;"> </span>31,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.25pt;"> </span>2019,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.3pt;"> </span>conformity<span style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </span>with<span style="letter-spacing:-0.2pt;"> </span>accounting<span style="letter-spacing:-0.15pt;"> </span>principles<span style="letter-spacing:-0.15pt;"> </span>generally<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>accepted in the United States of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </span>America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:3.49%;font-size:10pt;letter-spacing:0.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#8220;PCAOB&#8221;), the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019, based on criteria established in Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework: (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#8220;COSO&#8221;), and our report dated February 28, 2020, expressed an unqualified<span style="letter-spacing:-0.3pt;"> </span>opinion.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.58%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis for Opinion</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:3.49%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>an<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>opinion<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>on<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>Company's<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>financial<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>statements<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>based<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>on<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>our<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>audits.<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span><span style="letter-spacing:0.25pt;">We</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>are<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>a<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>public<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:3.49%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:5.04%;text-indent:-0.84%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Critical Audit Matters</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The critical audit matters communicated below are matters arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that were communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relate to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>challenging,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>subjective,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>or<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>complex<span style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </span>judgments.<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>The<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>communication<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.3pt;"> </span>critical<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>audit<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>matters<span style="letter-spacing:-0.35pt;"> </span>does not<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>alter<span style="letter-spacing:1.9pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>any<span style="letter-spacing:1.8pt;"> </span>way<span style="letter-spacing:1.85pt;"> </span>our<span style="letter-spacing:2.15pt;"> </span>opinion<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>on<span style="letter-spacing:1.95pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>financial<span style="letter-spacing:1.95pt;"> </span>statements,<span style="letter-spacing:1.85pt;"> </span>taken<span style="letter-spacing:1.9pt;"> </span>as<span style="letter-spacing:2.05pt;"> </span>a<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>whole,<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>we<span style="letter-spacing:1.95pt;"> </span>are<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>not,<span style="letter-spacing:2pt;"> </span>by communicating the critical audit matters below, providing separate opinions on the critical audit matters or on the accounts or disclosures to which they relate.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.2%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Valuation of Acquired Intangible Assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>disclosed<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>Note<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>4<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>to<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>financial<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>statements,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>during<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.45pt;"> </span>year<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>ended<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>December<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>31,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>2019,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>Company finalized the purchase price allocation for two 2018 acquisitions with aggregate consideration of $521.5 million. In 2018, the Company acquired all of the outstanding equity of SCVNGR, Inc. d/b/a LevelUp (&#8220;LevelUp&#8221;) for consideration of $369.4 million and Tapingo Ltd. (&#8220;Tapingo&#8221;) for consideration of $152.1 million.<span style="letter-spacing:1.35pt;"> </span>These<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>acquisitions<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>resulted<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>Company<span style="letter-spacing:-0.85pt;"> </span>recognizing<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>$57.5<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>million<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>in<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>acquired<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>intangible<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>assets, comprised of $36.5 million of acquired intangible assets from the LevelUp acquisition and $21.0 million of intangible assets acquired from the Tapingo<span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span>acquisition.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:5.65%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As described in Note 2 <span style="font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, Intangible Assets </span>and Note 4 <span style="font-style:italic;">Acquisitions, Additional information</span>&#59; the valuation of acquired intangible assets is based on the estimated fair values at acquisition as measured by a combination of income, cost, and market approaches. The valuation of the acquired intangible assets involved a significant level of judgment and estimation by management including the selection of valuation models and the estimation of key inputs for the various valuation models employed, such as discount rates, estimated future cash flows, initial developer costs, expected<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>profits,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>royalty<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>rates,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>rates<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>attrition,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>expected<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>rates<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>return.<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>Due<span style="letter-spacing:-0.55pt;"> </span>to<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>complexity<span style="letter-spacing:-0.8pt;"> </span>of<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>these estimates, the Company engaged a specialist to assist in </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">70</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the valuation of acquired intangible assets. </span><span style="letter-spacing:0.25pt;">We </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">considered auditing the valuation of acquired intangible assets for these acquisitions to be a critical audit matter, because it involved a high degree of subjectivity in evaluating management&#8217;s estimates and judgments as well as the use of valuation</span><span style="letter-spacing:-0.1pt;"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">specialists.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our audit procedures related to the valuation of acquired intangible assets included the following:</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Capitalization of Website and Software Development Costs</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s business is predominantly based upon revenue derived from connecting diners and restaurants through technology to create a takeout marketplace for restaurant pick-up and delivery orders and, as a result, the Company invests in website and software development. As described in Note 2 <span style="font-style:italic;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies, Website and Software Development Costs </span>and Note 7 <span style="font-style:italic;">Property</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span><span style="font-style:italic;">and</span><span style="font-style:italic;letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span><span style="font-style:italic;">Equipment</span>,<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>significant<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>internal<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>and<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>external<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>costs<span style="letter-spacing:-0.7pt;"> </span>incurred<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>during<span style="letter-spacing:-0.75pt;"> </span>the<span style="letter-spacing:-0.65pt;"> </span>application<span style="letter-spacing:-0.6pt;"> </span>development stage of website and software development, as well as certain enhancement costs incurred in the post- implementation phase that are determined to be substantial upgrades, are capitalized if determined by management to be direct and incremental thereto. During the year ended December 31, 2019, the Company capitalized $64.5 million of website and software development<span style="letter-spacing:-0.5pt;"> </span>costs.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The capitalization of website and software development costs involves a significant amount of judgment and estimation by management. Evaluating website and software development costs for capitalization involves assessing a variety of subjective factors and estimates, such as distinguishing between costs incurred during the preliminary project period and those incurred during the development stages of an application. Further, management applies significant judgment to identify website and software development costs that meet the capitalization criteria of being significant, and direct and incremental to the application development. In addition, the determination of capitalizable website and software development costs involves complexity in the aggregation and evaluation of significant amounts of data.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We considered auditing the amount of capitalized website and software development costs to be a critical audit matter, because it involved a significant amount of judgment and estimation by management as well as complexity in the aggregation and evaluation of significant amounts of data and thus required the application of significant auditor judgment.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our audit procedures related to the capitalized website and software development costs included the following procedures:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:3pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Tested the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls over the identification and calculation of website and software development costs to be capitalized as well as the completeness and accuracy of reports used in management&#8217;s<span style="letter-spacing:-0.4pt;"> </span>calculation.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Item</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;9A.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:18pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;" id="Controls_and_Procedures">Controls and Procedures </p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As required by Rule 13a-15(b) and Rule 15d-15(b) of the Exchange Act, the Company&#8217;s management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, is responsible for establishing and maintaining effective disclosure controls and procedures, as defined under Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) of the Exchange Act. As of December&#160;31, 2019, an evaluation was performed under the supervision and with the participation of management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures. Based on that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that disclosure controls and procedures as of December&#160;31, 2019 were effective in ensuring information required to be disclosed in the Company&#8217;s SEC reports was recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms, and that such information was accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There have not been any changes in the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act) that occurred during the quarter ended December&#160;31, 2019 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management&#8217;s Report and Attestation Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act). </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019. Our management based this assessment on criteria for effective internal control over financial reporting described in the &#8220;Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework (2013)&#8221; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Based on this assessment, our management determined that, as of December 31, 2019, the Company maintained effective internal control over financial reporting.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Crowe LLP, our independent registered public accounting firm, who has audited the consolidated financial statements of the Company included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and as part of the audit, has issued an attestation report on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019.</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">73</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="REPORT_OF_INDEPENDENT_2"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders of</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Grubhub Inc. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Chicago, Illinois</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Opinion on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited Grubhub Inc.&#8217;s (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019, based on criteria established in Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework: (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (&#8220;COSO&#8221;). In our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2019<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">, </span>based on criteria established in Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework: (2013) issued by COSO.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We also have audited, <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&#8220;PCAOB&#8221;), the consolidated balance sheets of the Company as of December 31, </span>2019<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;"> and </span>2018<span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income (loss), changes in stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, </span>2019, <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">and the related notes (collectively referred to as the "financial statements")</span> and <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">our report dated February 28, 2020 expressed an unqualified opinion. </span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis for Opinion</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s management<span style="font-family:Arial;"> </span>is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#8217;s Report and Attestation Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&#160;&#160;Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.&#160;&#160;We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> <span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. </span><span style="color:#000000;">Our audit also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Definition and Limitations of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:6pt;text-indent:4.54%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&#160;&#160;A company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company&#59; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company&#59; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.74%;text-indent:5.06%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements.&#160;&#160;Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.74%;text-indent:5.06%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
